_about: The UI languages, in the order of the Magic Rampage Companion app's picker and of Penumbra's Languages.hpp: en (the default) de es fr it pt ru tr uk ja ar.
sim/Strings.hpp's Lang enum has exactly these codes in exactly this order, and the load is refused otherwise. name_native is the language's own name in its own script (the picker draws it).

font_set: 'original' = the strings lie inside the original fonts' Latin-1 set (U+0020-007E, U+00A0-00FF), which the tests check; 'generated' = every font slot is drawn from a face the fonts step makes at run time.

fonts: how a 'generated' language is drawn (planning step 237, sim/FontBake): faces are the committed .ttf files of game/data/fonts (their OFL texts beside them), scripts are code point ranges (hex, inclusive) that route to a face of their own, and each slot is one of the original's font slots whose look the baked atlas reproduces. A code point in no script is drawn from the slot's text_face. Every language whose font_set is 'generated' is drawn by the same routing.
Never name a generated .fnt or .png here: tools/package/closure.py resolves such a name as an original asset and refuses the package.

Every number below says where it came from. 'measured' = read off the original's font files in reference/extracted/assets/data (never copied: only the numbers are here); 'fitted' = least squares against the original's atlas; 'chosen' = a look decision made by eye against the original, tunable.

line_height, base, padding and spacing are the original's .fnt files' own (info padding=, spacing=, common lineHeight= and base=), so the baked fonts take the place of the original's with no change to any placement.
cap_height is the height of a capital H above the baseline in the original: the .fnt's base minus (the H glyph's yoffset plus the padding above it), measured on the glyph's opaque pixels.

shadow: the original's glyph carries a soft black shadow under it. dx, dy, sigma and alpha were FITTED to the visible shadow of twelve glyphs of each atlas (H A X o e d 2 8 a t P m): the glyph's own coverage moved by (dx, dy) and blurred by a Gaussian of sigma, at alpha of black.

chosen by eye (Step 237, the contact sheet against the original's 'Part 21'): embolden 0.6 of a pixel for Matura's slot, because Kurale Regular is far lighter than Matura MT Script Capitals Bold (0 keeps the face's own weight; the glyph grows a pixel at most on each side), and the Japanese face's reference ratio 1.0, the kanji for 'day' as tall as a capital.

Faces: Kurale (Matura's slot) is the nearest open-licence look to Matura's swash capitals; Noto Sans Bold stands in for Verdana Bold; Noto Sans JP and Noto Sans Arabic carry their scripts in both slots. Each face is sized so that its reference glyph is reference_height times the slot's cap height: the capital H for the Latin faces, the kanji for 'day' (U+65E5) for Japanese, the alef (U+0627) for Arabic.
